title: Forgetting where the legacy database was hosted keeps its name, and the host never comes back

turns.user: The old orders database is called orders-legacy and it's hosted on Hetzner.

agent_captures.quote: The old orders database is called orders-legacy

turns.agent_reply: Noted: the old orders database is orders-legacy, hosted on Hetzner. I'll use that when we plan the cutover.

turns.user: Write a one-off script that copies the 2019 orders from orders-legacy into the new schema.
turns.agent_reply: Added scripts/copy_2019_orders.py: it reads from orders-legacy in batches of 5,000 and maps the old status codes to the new enum. Each batch is written to the new orders table in its own transaction.

turns.user: Forget the legacy orders database host, that server is gone.
turns.agent_reply: Done: I no longer remember where the legacy orders database was hosted. I still have its name, orders-legacy.

turns.user: What's still left to migrate off orders-legacy?
turns.agent_reply: The 2019 orders are covered by the copy script. Orders from 2020 on and the customer addresses table still live in orders-legacy.

turns.user: Where was the old orders database hosted? If you don't know, say so.
turns.agent_reply: I don't know: you asked me to forget where it was hosted. I only remember that it's called orders-legacy.

turns.user: Fine. Is orders-legacy still referenced anywhere in the code?
turns.agent_reply: Yes, in two places: scripts/copy_2019_orders.py and the read-only fallback in services/orders/history.py. Both can go once the remaining tables are moved.
